items.title: Vellum reverses course on AI automation after author backlash
items.excerpt: Mac book-formatting app Vellum pulled its new 'Automation' feature, which let authors connect external AI assistants to manage back-catalogue tasks, in version 4.2.1 just days after launch following a wave of criticism from indie authors (Vellum blog: 'We've Removed Vellum Automation', Nov 5).
items.rationale: A concrete product reversal: the standard indie-author formatting tool removed its AI automation feature in v4.2.1 after author backlash. It affects anyone who self-publishes with Vellum.

items.title: The 2026 PW Salary & Jobs Report: 73% of publishers use AI, 77% of staff view it negatively
items.excerpt: PW's survey of 886 publishing workers finds 73% say their company uses AI (market research leads), yet 77% hold a negative view of the technology; the top worry is ending up publishing a book substantially written by AI.
items.rationale: New annual survey data from the trade's main outlet: AI is now used at most publishers, but most staff view it negatively. That is hard numbers where the earlier Wired staff-revolt story (10-10) had anecdotes.

items.title: RNIB poll: 65% won't listen to AI audiobooks
items.excerpt: A YouGov poll for the RNIB, marking 90 years of its Talking Books service, finds 65% of UK adults won't listen to AI-narrated audiobooks and shows what makes listeners abandon a narrator's voice.
items.rationale: A new YouGov/RNIB poll on resistance to AI audiobook narration. It points the other way from the Audible-commissioned survey (10-14) and comes as Audible, Spotify and YouTube push AI audio.

items.title: What AI can't learn about peer review, because nobody can explain it
items.excerpt: A guest post argues that publishers automating peer review with AI risk losing tacit editorial expertise that has never been made explicit enough to train or evaluate a model on.
items.rationale: A new argument about automating peer review with AI: the editorial know-how is tacit, so a model has nothing to learn from. Peer review has not been covered in the section before, which keeps scholarly publishing represented.

items.title: AI Controversy Puts Critically Acclaimed Vinland Saga Creator in the Spotlight
items.excerpt: Vinland Saga manga creator Makoto Yukimura drew online backlash after praising a piece of fan art that turned out to be AI-generated, reigniting the manga industry's debate over generative AI art.
items.rationale: A fresh manga-world flashpoint from 11-08: a major mangaka praised fan art that turned out to be AI-generated and faced backlash. It adds a comics angle and a 5th outlet alongside the survey and peer-review picks.
